newsitem.title: HONG KONG: McDonough sees dlr gain importance in EMU run-up.
newsitem.headline: McDonough sees dlr gain importance in EMU run-up.

text.p: New York Federal Reserve Bank president William McDonough said on Tuesday the U.S. dollar may become more important as a reserve currency in the run-up to and the years following the establishment of a single European currency.
"A brand new currency is going to have to develop the support that the deutschemark has," McDonough told a conference in Hong Kong.
"The dollar may take on a bit more relative importance as a reserve currency" in the run up to and during the first couple of years after the establishment of a single European currency, he said.
McDonough said he had every reason to believe the Euro would gain support that the German mark has.
He said the dollar will continue to serve as a major reserve currency, and noted that the U.S. currency was "behaving particularly well".
